title: Dependency flight-path & clearance protocol for cross-team roadmap lanes
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a standardized 'flight-path' metaphor and procedural clearance protocol to manage roadmap dependencies across Engineering, Design, Security, and Infrastructure. The goal is to reduce manual triage, provide predictable handoff windows, and automate early warnings for cross-team blockers that affect quarter-level OKRs and initiative milestones.
acceptance_criteria: A clear flight-path status model (Cleared / Holding / Emergency Hold / Diverted) documented and adopted by 4 teams (Eng, Design, Security, Infra)
Automated Slack + email escalation when a dependency moves to Holding for >72 hours or when cumulative lead time risk exceeds threshold in the dependency ledger
Integration with roadmap dashboard so each initiative shows dependency clearance status and next required action
Two pilot initiatives successfully use the protocol for a full planning cycle (planning -> canary -> cutover) without any missed handoffs
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Eng/Design/Security/Infra leads. Collected current pain points: noisy dependency lists, unclear owners for mid-sprint unblock, and lack of automated reminders.
2026-02-26: Prototype status model proposed in workshop: Cleared / Pre-Clear / Holding / Emergency Hold / Diverted. Agreed on SLAs for Pre-Clear (48h) and Holding (72h) before escalation.
2026-03-01: Drafted Confluence doc for flight-path protocol and mapping to existing release gates. Added example flows for design handoff and security review windows.
2026-03-04: PM leadership approved pilot for two initiatives (Console observability improvements, Dedicated autoscale policy). Eng and Security committed resources for pilot planning.
2026-03-05: Submitted a short RFC to infra-team for webhook support from our dependency ledger to trigger Slack workflows (PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/198).
decisions: Adopt flight-path metaphor rather than severity buckets to make cross-functional handoffs more intuitive for non-engineering stakeholders
Implement 2-tier escalation: automated reminders at 48/72 hours, then a live sync request to owners if unresolved after 96 hours
Map status to release gates: Holding/Emergency Hold blocks canary and must be resolved before cutover unless executive waiver provided
open_risks: Teams may mark too many dependencies as Cleared prematurely to avoid escalation; need acceptance criteria per clearance type
Lack of webhook support from legacy infra components could delay automation; fall back to scheduled scans of dependency ledger
Security review SLAs vary widely depending on classification; need a short-run policy for pilot initiatives to prevent indefinite holds
notes_for_engineering: Need a stable webhook or API for the dependency ledger so infra can push Slack notifications with context and owner links
Provide a small endpoint that returns current clearance status + last updated timestamp to support UI badges
Estimate ~3 days for basic webhook + endpoint for pilot without SLA guarantees
notes_for_design: Create compact UI badges for initiative cards showing flight-path status and days-in-state
Design a lightweight modal to surface required next action for owners with quick links to PRs, audit logs, and security issues
notes_for_security: Define a short-form security intake checklist for pilots: classification, minimum mitigations, estimated review time
Agree to a handshake window (48h) where security can request additional info before marking Holding
For pilot initiatives security will allocate one SME for synchronous unblock calls during the first two sprints
